units.text: We'll choose a deployment by the target before picking a rollout curve. E C two supports in-place and blue-green. For on-premises instances, use in-place; blue-green on the shared compute platform requires Amazon E C two instances.

CodeDeploy changes different targets for Lambda and E C S. With Lambda it moves alias traffic between versions. In the CodeDeploy E C S model, the load balancer moves traffic between task sets. Don't apply an E C two instance update recipe to either.

For an in-place E C two deployment, update a batch while the remaining healthy capacity serves requests. The hooks apply the revision and validate the instances. Confirm enough healthy capacity stays available before moving to another batch.
If an updated instance fails its checks, stop or follow the configured rollback path. Reinstalling an earlier revision does not automatically reverse data changes or other external effects.

Blue-green prepares a separate fleet and validates it before shifting load balancer traffic. The old fleet can remain available for a configured period. That buys a traffic recovery option at the cost of extra capacity during the overlap.

Check when the old fleet is deregistered or terminated, and whether you can safely route traffic back. Do not assume a retained fleet is immediately serving, or that a traffic rollback resolves incompatible data changes.
